input.question: If the word "sum" is used to describe the total amount of *something* that exists, why is "sum total" so common in vocabulary? Isn't it like saying "total total"?
input.ground_truth: Sum only indicates that a summation has taken place (things have been added together). If you have multiple partial sums within the context (such as multiple subtotals on a receipt), the sum total unambiguously refers to the total of all of the sums, rather than one of the partial sums.
